I'll take capitalism under the following definition:

Government guarantees 'negative' rights: no one can kill me or take my stuff or shut me up if I'm talking on my own or public land. If they do, the government will punish them.

However, the government doesn't guarantee any 'positive' rights: no one has any obligations to do anything for me other than leaving me alone (not actively harm me). I'm not guaranteed healthcare or food or a private phone line. I have to negotiate that with other citizens that I have no power to compel just as they have no power to compel me.

If I see a market underserved by the existing rail or phone providers then I can build a lot of good will (quantifiable in dollars) by undertaking to build a better system myself. E.g., phone lines with end to end encryption that I can't eavesdrop with mathematical certainty. Everyone around me (other than the incumbents) is likewise incentivized to fix any such problem.

As the government tries to guarantee positive rights the pool of ideas and people excited to implement them shrinks. The government can't help but over-prescribe--too many people want gibs and will use the government as a proxy to enact violence if someone doesn't provide them. This is true no matter which system you live under but my preference would be to live with people who at least aspire to peace (including not using the government for gibs).
